turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
They... my lieutenant sent me here. I was at the station. Just moving the airway bags around. I had to put them in a pattern I knew was right. And... I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud. 

He told me to stop and step away, but I wouldn't. I couldn't. If I broke the sequence... the whole bay would go bad. So they made me come here.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes engaging in abnormal, inappropriate behavior at work (arranging bags, repeating numbers) and refusing to stop when ordered by a superior (negativism).
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes performing repetitive behaviors (arranging bags in a specific pattern, repeating numbers out loud) to prevent a feared, unrealistic consequence ('the whole bay would go bad').

turns.doctor_question: When you say the whole bay would go bad, did you know that might just be your mind telling you that, or were you certain it would really happen?
turns.patient_response:
It wasn't my mind. I was certain. 

Because I... I already know what they're doing to me. The injury review people. Some of the supervisors, too. They've been watching me through the station cameras. And they... they go in and change my triage notes. Just to make me look unsafe. They keep telling me it's just routine paperwork, but... I know. I know they're doing it. So, yeah. I was certain.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses absolute certainty in a fixed, persecutory belief that supervisors are watching them through cameras and altering their notes to make them look unsafe, despite being told it is just routine paperwork.
